full_judgment:
2. Facts leading to the filing this appeal are that respondent No.1 as the preemptor filed Miscellaneous Case No.22 of 1997 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Phultala, Khulna under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950(the Act, 1950) for preemption of the case land as fully described in the schedule to the pre-emption application. 

 "Mr. Md. Nurul Amin, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners submitted that the pre-emptor totally failed to prove her date of knowledge by adducting competent witness. The P.W.2 did not state in his evidence that on 21.04.1997 the emptee Nos.1 and 2 disclosed firstly about their purchase. Besides, there is no other corroborative witness regarding the date of knowledge. The learned Advocate further submitted that the pre-emption case was filed on 09.06.1997 and P.W.2 was examined on 26.01.1999. P.W.2 stated in his evidence that Moslem and Mohabbat constructed new house before two years. If so, the date of knowledge of the petitioner was 26.01.1997 but the pre-emption case was filed on 09.06.1997. So, it is apparent from that the evidence of P.W.2 the pre-emption case was not filed within 4 months from the date of knowledge and as such, the High Court Division appears to have erred in law in not holding that the pre-emption case is barred by law of limitation." 

 9. From the order of the trial Court, it appears that it gave clear finding that the preemption application was barred by limitation. Admittedly, the preemption application was filed after 4(years), 2(Two) Months and 26(Twenty six) days. The pre-emptor stated in her application for pre-emption that she came to know about the transfer in question on 21.04.1997, when the pre-emptees (opposite party Nos.1 and 2 in the miscellaneous case) brought bricks and other construction materials to the case land. The case of the pre-emptees was that they took possession of the case land immediately after the kabala was executed and registered and erected kacha ghar therein. Subsequently, the construction of a building was almost completed. On behalf of the pre-emptor, two witnesses were examined and of them, PW1 was the pre-emptor herself and PW2 was one Karol Islam. The trial Court considering the testimony of PW2 in his examination -in-chief that the pre-emptees erected a new room on the case land, held that the testimony of Pw2 proved the fact that there were other rooms of the preemptees in the case land. The trial Court further observed that the pre-emptor could take step for holding local investigation to prove the fact that, in fact, the pre-emptees brought bricks and other construction materials to the case land on 21.04.1997 and that on that date, they had no room in the case land, but no step was taken on behalf of the pre-emptor in that respect, The trial Court further, held that PW2 admitted in his cross -examination that the construction of a building was completed upto lintel level, but the pre-emptor did not say anything about the said statement of PW2. The trial Court further observed that the pre-emptor could also hold local investigation to prove the fact that the construction of the building in the case land was done either on 21.04.1997 or thereafter, but she did not take any step in that respect. And this failure proved that the pre-emptor was aware of the kabala under preemption as well as the possession of the pre-emptees in the case land. But, in spite of that, she did not file the preemption application within time and filed the same long after 4(four) years, 2(two) months and 26 (twenty sis) days, so the preemption application was barred by limitation. The Appellate Court being the last Court of fact while affirming the order of the trial Court considered the evidence on record. 

 11. We have gone through the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 in fact, it is only PW1 who stated that she came to know about the transfer in question on 21.04.1997, but her testimony was not corroborated by PW2. What PW2 stated was that the pre emptees constructed a new room in the case land 2(two) years before and that the construction work of the room was completed upto lintel level. This PW was examined on 26.01.1999 and 2(two) years before means 26.01.1997, but the preemption application was filed on 09.06.1997, i.e. even if the testimony of PW2 is accepted, it would appear that the case was filed long after 4(four) months of the said construction made by the pre-emptees. Therefore, the High Court Division was totally wrong in finding that the preemption application was filed within time. The High Court Division made a fundamental mistake in stating that the preemption case was filed within the statutory period of 30 days of her knowledge, but, in fact, long after 4(four) months of the date of bringing the construction materials on the case land as stated by PW2. 

 13. The High Court Division also failed to consider that as the preemption application was filed long after 4(four) years, 2(two) months and 26(twenty Six) days from the date of transfer in question, the onus to prove the date of knowledge as stated by the pre-emptor in her application was heavily upon her and when both the Courts below on discussion of the evidence on record held that the pre-emptor failed to prove her date of knowledge of the kabala in question on 21.04.1997, it ought not to have interfered with such finding of fact. In the context, it may be repeated that except the pre-emptor herself, none corroborated the date of her knowledge of the transfer in question.
